moat: Corn germplasm and DEKALB brand
Advantage

'We are the main breeders in the country'; corn seed nearly doubled in FY21-25 (Rs 514 cr to Rs 914 cr, ~15% a year); 4 hybrids notified by the national maize programme and 8 PVP certificates in FY26; fully backward integrated.
The best business inside the company: growing, higher margin, tax-exempt.
Access to Bayer AG's patented molecules
Advantage
Indian launches of parent chemistry (Council Activ now a top-2/3 product; Plenexos and Xivana Smart in the pipeline); products from the last 3 years ~1/6 of crop-protection sales.
Keeps a premium portfolio, but timing is set by the parent and CIBRC registrations.
Brands and regulatory standing
Advantage
Roundup, Nativo, Laudis, Council Activ and DEKALB named as top brands (Nov-2025); management cites 'domain equity' with regulators.
Supports pricing in branded segments.
Distribution
Parity
3,534 distributors billed in FY26 (3,940 in FY25), top-10 13% of sales; the East moved to partners (Better Life Farming) to cut cost.
Wide but being pruned; not a barrier peers cannot match.
Cost position
Disadvantage
50% of purchases from related parties (Bayer AG Rs 1,341 cr in FY26), 'over-proportionally' from strong-currency countries; FY25 margins collapsed when Chinese generics capped prices.
Margins depend on the parent's transfer prices and sourcing shift.
Own R&D
Partial
R&D 2.0% of revenue, mostly corn breeding; no molecule discovery in India.
Seed R&D is real; chemistry innovation is borrowed.
Balance sheet and payout
Advantage
Net cash ~Rs 1,400 cr (Mar-26), no debt, ~95-100% payout, ROE ~24%.
Cash returns to shareholders, but leaves no war chest for growth.
critiques: Crop protection is ex-growth: CP ex-Roundup grew 5.8% a year in FY21-25 and the 3-5 year aspiration relies on corn doubling
Investor meet Nov-2025 (Kotak MF question); GAM
Margins are set by the parent's transfer prices: purchases from Bayer AG halved in FY26 and margins rose; the 'local sourcing' lever is slow and the parent decides it
HSBC and Unifi questions, Nov-2025 meet
Q1FY27 profit growth (+15%) came from a one-off Rs 63.9 cr gain; underlying profit fell ~2% on revenue -4%
Receivable risk: FY25 ECL provision Rs 78 cr ('unprecedented' collection issues); a weak season can repeat it
Tax: Rs 233 cr agricultural-income dispute; losing it would raise the 19-20% tax rate
Corn could be disrupted by duty-free US corn imports or GM approval that favours other trait owners; incremental seed production costs rise
The 2026 monsoon ended 12.6% below normal and El Nino is expected to persist into the rabi
